name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. A colonial hill station with pine-clad hills, vibrant markets, music culture, and base for exploring waterfalls, caves, and villages.
facts: Named after the sacred Shillong Peak
Nearest major airport is Guwahati (~100-120 km)
Famous for rock music scene and Police Bazaar

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India, dropping about 340 metres (1,115 ft) into a turquoise pool near Sohra (Cherrapunji) in East Khasi Hills. Fed by plateau rainwater; associated with a local legend of a woman named Likai.
facts: Plunge pool has distinctive green hue

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tier waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong in Upper Shillong area, East Khasi Hills. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew; named for a former elephant-shaped rock. Easily accessible with steps to each level.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city centre

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Cleanest village in Asia (awarded 2003), a picturesque Khasi village in East Khasi Hills near the Bangladesh border. Known for 100% literacy, bamboo dustbins, living root bridge nearby, and eco-tourism practices.
facts: Awarded Cleanest Village in Asia in 2003

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills, formed by guided aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees over generations by Khasi people. Requires a steep trek of ~3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: Trek starts at Tyrna near Sohra

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint and ridge in East Khasi Hills, about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Offers panoramic views of deep valleys, sometimes called the Grand Canyon of Meghalaya; popular for photography and short treks.
facts: Means end of hills in Khasi

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located ~10 km south of Shillong in East Khasi Hills. Sacred to the Khasi people as the abode of U Lei Shillong; offers panoramic views of the city, hills, and distant plains.
facts: IAF radar station requires ID for entry

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village in East Khasi Hills, protected for centuries by Khasi tradition. Untouched primary forest with monoliths, ritual sites, and high biodiversity; visitors may not remove anything.
facts: Site of historical coronation and rituals
One of the best-known sacred groves in Meghalaya

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Illuminated limestone show cave near Mawsmai village, about 6 km from Sohra (Cherrapunji) in East Khasi Hills. Features stalactites, stalagmites, and narrow passages; first electrified show cave in the region.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented seven-part waterfall near Mawsmai village in East Khasi Hills, dropping about 315 metres over limestone cliffs. Also known as Seven Sisters Falls; spectacular in monsoon, with views toward the Bangladesh plains.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous town and sub-division in East Khasi Hills, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to numerous waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints overlooking the plains of Bangladesh.
facts: Base for exploring southern plateau attractions

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, East Khasi Hills, created in 1894. Surrounded by botanical gardens, cobblestone paths, a wooden bridge, and boating facilities; locally known as Nan Polok.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Mawlai, Shillong (East Khasi Hills) showcasing the cultures, artefacts, music, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across seven floors and multiple galleries.

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning plunge waterfall near Amlarem in West Jaintia Hills with distinctive turquoise-blue pool, limestone cliffs and short scenic trail. Popular for swimming (life jackets available), photography and nature views; about 30 km from Jowai and 90 km from Shillong.
facts: About 30 km from Jowai and 90 km from Shillong
Turquoise pool suitable for swimming with facilities
Short trek from viewpoint to base

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of megalithic stones in Meghalaya at Nartiang village, West Jaintia Hills. Features upright menhirs (moo shynrang) and flat dolmens (moo kynthai) erected 16th-19th centuries to honor Jaintia kings and warriors; tallest around 8 metres. Summer capital remnants of Jaintia kingdom.
facts: Largest monolith collection in Khasi-Jaintia Hills
Tallest menhir about 8 metres erected by U Mar Phalyngki
About 24 km from Jowai and 60 km from Shillong

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Shakti Peeth temple in Nartiang dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti). One of 51 Shakta pithas where Sati's left thigh is believed to have fallen; important pilgrimage site for Shaktism devotees, especially during Durga Puja. Features traditional architecture near monoliths.
facts: Shakti worshipped as Jayanti, Bhairava as Kamadishwar

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake near Mukhla on NH-6, about 8-10 km from Jowai. According to legend dug with bow ends by followers of rebel chieftain Sajar Nangli to commemorate clan exodus; scenic picnic and boating spot amid pine forests.
facts: Also known as Pung Sajar Nangli
Legend of creation by Sajar Nangli's clans

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tier waterfall about 5-8 km from Jowai on Shillong-Jowai Road. Cascades over rocky cliffs into a pool with views over paddy valleys; accessible via arch bridge and short walk, often compared to Elephant Falls.
facts: Accessible via arch bridge over paddy fields
Popular for photography and short visits

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and crystal-clear Umngot River in West Jaintia Hills, famous for transparent waters where boats appear to float in air during dry season. Features 1932 British suspension bridge, boating, and India-Bangladesh border views; gateway to Shnongpdeng.
facts: Umngot River becomes transparent in winter

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village on the Umngot River about 8 km from Dawki, popular for adventure activities including kayaking, cliff jumping, camping, snorkelling and ziplining. Quieter alternative with sandy banks, clear waters and eco-tourism facilities.
facts: Offers kayaking, camping and adventure sports

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Scenic riverside spot meaning 'golden flower' on the Myntdu River near Jowai. Historical site where freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah initiated resistance against British rule; features suspension bridge, fish sanctuary elements, picnic areas and valley views.
facts: Site of U Kiang Nangbah freedom struggle

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai known for sacred grove, panoramic views of Pynthor Wah valley and Myntdu River. Developed for eco-tourism with walking paths, viewpoints and natural surroundings ideal for family outings and photography.
facts: Views of Pynthor Wah valley and Myntdu River
Popular local picnic and nature spot

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered secluded waterfall near Jarain/Shkentalang in West Jaintia Hills with clear blue plunge pool. Requires moderate trek through forest and rocky paths; less crowded hidden gem ideal for swimming and nature immersion, about 20 km from Jowai.
facts: About 20 km from Jowai near Jarain
Less crowded alternative to major falls

name: Thlu Muwi Stone Bridge
description: Historic megalithic stone bridge over the Muwi stream about 16 km from Jowai on Jowai-Dawki road. Built by warriors under Jaintia kings for royal passage from Jaintiapur to summer capital Nartiang; adjacent to Muwi Waterfalls, showcasing traditional granite slab construction.
facts: Built for Jaintia kings' travel to Nartiang
About 16 km from Jowai on Dawki road

name: Jowai Town
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district, a plateau town at about 1,380 m elevation surrounded by the Myntdu River. Cultural and commercial hub for Pnar (Jaintia) community, gateway to local waterfalls, lakes, monoliths and Behdeinkhlam festival.
facts: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills since 2012 district formation
Base for exploring district attractions and festivals
